rule: section 2 (cross-reference-dependent -- the DECISIVE ground), section 2 / section 3.8.1 / section 8.8 (no obligation-bearing clause -- copular 'shall be deemed' status class), section 3.5 / section 8.8 (non-party subject -- subject is a thing)
reason:
Confidentiality cross-reference clause. Two sentences, ZERO obligation-bearing clauses, so section 2's "contains 1-3 obligation-bearing clauses" eligibility test fails at zero and the segment is excluded whole. S1 [0:19] is the heading fragment "5.1Confidentiality." -- no subject, no modal, not a sentence in section 2.6's sense (the same leading-marker shape locked segment E02-006 records for its own "b) ", absorbed rather than logged as a class of its own). S2 [20:326] is the only modal-bearing sentence in the segment; "shall" occurs exactly once and its two predicates are "shall be deemed" and the coordinated "[shall be] ... subject to".

THREE INDEPENDENT GROUNDS. Each stands alone; the third is the decisive one and is stated first for that reason, because it closes off the counter-reading that the other two do not have to reach.

GROUND 1 -- CROSS-REFERENCE-DEPENDENT (section 2, on the v0.28 scored-field-dependence test), AND THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING GROUND. The second conjunct's entire operative content is "subject to the confidentiality provisions set forth in Article 12 of the Collaboration and License Agreement" -- a DIFFERENT AGREEMENT, which is not in this corpus. PROVEN MECHANICALLY RATHER THAN ASSERTED, the same discipline batch 4's C04-051 exclusion used for its own "6-month period" anaphor: "Article 12" occurs EXACTLY ONCE in all 54,541 characters of E03, and that one occurrence IS the reference itself. E03's own article headings run 1-11 and 14; it has no Article 12 of its own. So nothing in the corpus resolves it.

Section 2's test is whether "a scored field's value (section 5's eight clauses) cannot be determined without resolving the reference", and here EVERY scored field fails it: action, object_class, obligee, temporal and conditions are all unreadable without Article 12, and no agent is named for the imported duty at all -- "such Party" is the DISCLOSER, not the party who would owe confidentiality. PRECEDENT CALIBRATION against the six committed cross-reference exclusions rather than argued in the abstract: this is C15-046's and C11-079's shape (the out-of-segment reference carries OPERATIVE CONTENT), not C03-01 item 4's ("as set forth in the terms of the Maintenance Addendum", reviewer-confirmed as qualifying SCOPE DETAIL ONLY and therefore keepable). It is in fact stronger than any of the six: those reference another part of the SAME document, this references another AGREEMENT.

WHY THIS GROUND IS RECORDED IN FULL RATHER THAN FOLDED INTO THE NARROW BATCH-3 COPULAR WORDING (reviewer instruction, 2026-09-24). The strongest reading AGAINST excluding is that "subject to the confidentiality provisions" imports a real duty on the receiving party to keep the Information confidential. Grounds 2 and 3 do not engage that reading -- they say the clause as written states a status. THIS ground defeats it even if it is granted in full, because a duty whose action, object, recipient, timing and conditions all live in an out-of-corpus document cannot be annotated whatever its deontic force. A future session reading a shorter citation could reasonably take this for "just another copular exclusion" and reopen it on exactly that counter-reading; it is written out here so that it does not have to be rediscovered.

GROUND 2 -- COPULAR DEEMING, NOT COMMANDED CONDUCT (section 2, section 3.8.1, section 8.8). "shall be deemed Confidential Information of such Party" assigns a classification; nobody is told to do, or to refrain from doing, an act. Section 3.8.1's branch-1 exclusion list already names this class directly with its own worked instance ("the Gas shall be deemed 'dry'"), and three exclusions are committed in it: E08-046 ("shall be deemed to have been so delivered"), C06-022 ("shall be deemed to be in compliance") and C17-038 ("shall survive"). C06-022 IS THE HARDER PRECEDENT AND IS CITED FOR THAT REASON: its grammatical subject IS a party (Purchaser) and it was still excluded, because the predicate asserts status -- the distinction section 8.8.1 draws for negated entitlement. Here the subject is not a party at all, so this clause is a weaker case for annotation than one already excluded.

GROUND 3 -- NON-PARTY SUBJECT (section 3.5, section 8.8). The subject is "Any and all Information disclosed by a Party" -- a thing. This is section 8.8's own named "non-party subject" class and the identical ground already committed at C22-045, C10-029 and C17-038, and applied as section 8.8.4's prior filter 2 at E07-010 ("These personnel shall also be responsible for..."), which sits inside a LOCKED segment. The two Parties appear in the sentence only as the source and the addressee of a disclosure, never as actors under a commanded duty.

NOT A DIFFICULTY DODGE, stated because section 2.1 step 4's rejection sample exists to catch exactly that. At 326 characters and one operative sentence this is the SHORTEST and most straightforward segment drawn in batch 5 so far -- excluding it buys no difficulty relief, and each of the three grounds is independent of difficulty in any case. The cheaper-looking alternative (annotating a one-clause item) is not available on any of the three.

PROVENANCE. Segment text reproduces byte-for-byte against both the live corpus pool rebuild (1,547 segments, the pool's own known-answer gate) and batch04/draw.json. E03 is one of the five EDGAR documents carrying the anti-bot script-tag injection tracked in CLAUDE.md; that injection is proven inert for derived artifacts and is inert here -- the pool rebuilds to 1,547 exactly and this segment is unchanged. The sentence split was produced by corpus.split_sentences() gated first against locked segment E02-006's committed section 2.7 offsets (Standing Principle 7).

rule: section 2 (contains 1-3 obligation-bearing clauses -- FAILS AT ZERO); C1: section 2 / section 3.2 / section 8.8 (no obligation-bearing clause -- event-as-subject legal-effect statement); C2: section 2 (cross-reference-dependent -- the gating condition's TRUTH VALUE is unresolvable at span scope, REVIEWER-RULED 2026-09-24, refining C11-079's operative-content test; see observations)
reason:
Cross-agreement material-breach / termination clause. Two sentences, ZERO obligation-bearing clauses after both operative clauses are ruled, so section 2's "contains 1-3 obligation-bearing clauses" eligibility test FAILS AT ZERO and the segment is excluded whole.

RECONCILIATION, CONFIRMED MECHANICALLY RATHER THAN ASSERTED, because the disposition turns on the count being zero rather than one. S1 [0:19] "(a)Material Breach." carries no modal, no finite verb and no subject+predicate -- a heading fragment, not a clause in section 2.6's sense, absorbed the same way E03-037's "5.1Confidentiality." and locked segment E02-006's "b) " are. It does not change the count in either direction. S2 [20:420] is the only modal-bearing sentence and holds exactly two clauses, C1 [20:159] and C2 [164:420]; both are excluded below. 0 obligation-bearing clauses.

C1 -- NOT OBLIGATION-BEARING (section 2, section 3.2, section 8.8). "A Party's material breach of this Supply Agreement will constitute such Party's material breach of the Collaboration and License Agreement". The subject is "A Party's material breach" -- an EVENT, not a party -- and "will constitute" states a legal effect, not commanded conduct. Direct committed precedent: C02-062 ("no obligation-bearing clause -- subject is an event, savings/interpretive"), with section 3.2's will-future-fact rule and section 8.8's non-party-subject class both reaching the same result independently. Not contested.

C2 -- CROSS-REFERENCE-DEPENDENT (section 2), REVIEWER-RULED 2026-09-24, AND THE RULING REFINES THE TEST RATHER THAN MERELY APPLYING IT. See the observation below, which is the substantive record; this paragraph states the disposition only. "each Party shall have the right to terminate this Supply Agreement and the Collaboration and License Agreement for the other Party's uncured material breach of this Supply Agreement as set forth in Section 13.2.1 of the Collaboration and License Agreement" is excluded because the gating condition's TRUTH VALUE is not resolvable from the span: "uncured" is defined nowhere in this contract, and its entire content lives in Section 13.2.1 of an agreement that is not in this corpus.

WHAT C2 IS NOT EXCLUDED FOR, stated because each was checked and each fails, and because C2 is otherwise a strong item. (1) NOT section 2.5 / 2.5.1 (monitorable stakes): C2 has BOTH a correlative party ("the other Party") AND a gating condition, so it clears the test C04-026, C11-046 and C14-044#S1 each failed -- it is not a bare rights-reservation. (2) NOT section 8.8 or 8.8.1: the subject IS a party and "shall have the right to terminate" commands an exercisable act, not a status; this is the AFFIRMATIVE counterpart of section 8.8.1's negated entitlement and is not in that class. (3) NOT a taxonomy gap: TERMINATE is a member of ast.py's closed 34-verb ACTIONS, verified by reading it. (4) NOT unannotatable on its other fields -- modality MAY, action TERMINATE, obligor "each Party", obligee "the other Party", object_class agreement, temporal null are ALL readable in-span.

THE NEAR-MISS PRECEDENT IS A LOCKED ITEM, AND NAMING IT IS THE POINT. C13-03 -- "Either party shall have the right to terminate this Agreement effective upon written notice to the other party in the event the non-notifying party becomes insolvent..." -- is the same construction, same modality, same action, same object_class, and IS annotated. C2 differs from it in exactly one respect: C13-03's gating event ("becomes insolvent", "bankruptcy or insolvency proceedings are instituted") is FULLY STATED AND EVALUABLE IN-SPAN, while C2's ("uncured") is not. That single difference is the whole ground of this exclusion, and it is why this entry carries the observation below rather than a one-line rule citation.

NOT A DIFFICULTY DODGE, stated because section 2.1 step 4's rejection sample exists to catch exactly that. C2 is a clean, easy item on every field except the one that excludes it, and a draft of it was prepared in full and put to the reviewer before the ruling -- the cheaper move here would have been to KEEP it, not to exclude it. The exclusion was ruled against the drafter's own prepared item, not in place of preparing one.

PROVENANCE. Segment text reproduces byte-for-byte against both the live corpus pool rebuild (1,547 segments, the pool's own known-answer gate) and batch04/draw.json. Sentence split produced by corpus.split_sentences(), gated first against locked segment E02-006's committed section 2.7 offsets (Standing Principle 7). E03 is one of the five EDGAR documents carrying the anti-bot script-tag injection tracked in CLAUDE.md; it is inert here, as the pool rebuild and the byte-for-byte match both show.

observations.label: THE CROSS-REFERENCE TEST IS REFINED: the axis is the CONDITION'S TRUTH VALUE, not merely whether content sits outside the span
observations.status: REVIEWER-RULED 2026-09-24. Forward guidance in this log entry; NOT yet a guideline section (one instance).
observations.cross_reference: section 2 (cross-reference row, incl. its v0.28 verbatim-quotation carve-in); C11-079; C15-046; C03-01 item 4; C13-03 (locked contrast pair); section 5 clause 7
observations.note:
FIRST CASE DISTINGUISHING SECTION 2's CROSS-REFERENCE EXCLUSION FROM ITS OWN v0.28 VERBATIM-QUOTATION CARVE-IN. The guideline has never drawn this line, and a future similar case should cite this reasoning rather than rediscover it. Recorded as forward guidance in this exclusion's own log entry rather than cashed into a guideline section, on C14-139's established precedent for a ruling with one instance (section 14.4: repeated uncertainty is a missing rule; ONE instance is a logged ruling).

THE COLLISION, STATED AS BOTH HALVES BECAUSE SECTION 2's OWN ROW CONTAINS BOTH AND THEY POINT OPPOSITE WAYS HERE.
  EXCLUDING half: a cross-reference excludes when "a scored field's value (section 5's eight clauses) cannot be determined without resolving the reference" -- C11-079's shape, "the consent mechanism that gates the permission is outside the segment", ruled on OPERATIVE CONTENT.
  KEEPING half (v0.28, verbatim): "Mere presence does not exclude: a cross-reference inside text quoted VERBATIM -- in span_text, in a CONDITIONS ENTRY, or in a carve-out dropped under section 3.8.1 branch 3 -- requires no resolution and is annotatable."
C2 is the first item where the reference sits inside what would be a verbatim `conditions` entry AND supplies the mechanism that gates the permission. Read one way, clause 7 compares condition STRINGS so the field's value is fully determined by quoting and the item is annotatable. Read the other, the gate is outside and the item excludes. Both are citable; neither precedent (C11-079 excluding / C03-01 item 4 keeping) was ever distinguished on this axis.

THE DISCRIMINATOR, REVIEWER-RULED 2026-09-24 -- AND IT REFINES C11-079's TEST RATHER THAN SIMPLY APPLYING IT.

  DOES THE OUT-OF-CORPUS REFERENCE DEFINE A TERM THE CONDITION'S TRUTH VALUE DEPENDS ON, OR DOES IT MERELY SUPPLY PROCEDURAL MECHANICS ONCE THE CONDITION IS ALREADY KNOWN TO HOLD?
    - TRUTH VALUE depends on it  -> EXCLUDE. The condition cannot be evaluated at span scope at all, so `conditions` is unscoreable in substance however faithfully it is quoted.
    - PROCEDURAL MECHANICS only  -> the verbatim carve-in governs; quote it and annotate normally.

  WHY THIS IS SHARPER THAN "OPERATIVE CONTENT LIVES OUTSIDE" (C11-079's framing), AND WHY THAT MATTERS. "Operative content" is satisfied by almost any substantive reference, including purely procedural ones, so it cannot distinguish C11-079 from C03-01 item 4 without a further judgment the test does not supply -- which is exactly why those two precedents have sat side by side, cited as "operative content" versus "scope detail", with no stated axis between them. The real question is narrower and checkable: IS THE CONDITION'S TRUTH-CONDITION RESOLVABLE FROM THE SPAN? Not whether some content sits outside it. This does not overturn C11-079 -- it passes the sharper test too, since whether BKC's consent "be first obtained as provided below" is satisfied is exactly a truth-condition living outside -- but it states WHY it passes in terms that also explain why C03-01 item 4 does not.

  APPLIED TO C2, AND THE APPLICATION IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. The condition is "for the other Party's UNCURED material breach of this Supply Agreement". "Uncured" is not defined by this span, and NOT ANYWHERE IN THIS CONTRACT: "cure"/"uncured" occurs EXACTLY ONCE in all 54,541 characters of E03, in this very sentence. What notice must be given, how long the cure window runs, and what counts as cure are all in Section 13.2.1 of the Collaboration and License Agreement -- a DIFFERENT AGREEMENT, not in this corpus. "Section 13.2.1" likewise occurs EXACTLY ONCE in E03, inside the reference itself, so nothing in the corpus resolves it. The condition therefore has no truth value determinable at span scope, and the reference is not supplying mechanics for an already-known condition -- it is supplying the condition's entire content.

  THE CONTRAST PAIR IS A LOCKED ITEM, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THE AXIS REAL RATHER THAN A DISTINCTION INVENTED FOR THIS SEGMENT. C13-03's gating event -- "in the event the non-notifying party becomes insolvent or makes an assignment for the benefit of creditors, or in the event bankruptcy or insolvency proceedings are instituted" -- is fully stated and externally evaluable in-span; a monitor can determine whether it holds without leaving the segment, and C13-03 is annotated with exactly that text as its `conditions` entry. Same construction, same modality (MAY), same action (TERMINATE), same object_class (agreement). The ONLY difference is truth-condition resolvability, and it is decisive.

FORCING FUNCTION, stated so a future session does not have to re-derive when this becomes a guideline section: a SECOND instance -- most informatively one falling on the KEEPING side, where a reference inside a verbatim conditions entry supplies procedure only and the item is annotated over it. That would give the axis both of its cells, which this one instance does not. Until then this is a logged ruling with one instance, not a section.

SEARCH KEY: cross-reference, verbatim carve-in, conditions truth value, truth-condition resolvability, procedural mechanics, uncured, Section 13.2.1, C11-079, C03-01 item 4, C13-03, E03-046, C2.

span_text: provided, however, that the other party reserves the right to challenge such disclosure under applicable law.
rule: section 2 (savings/reservation provision -- no obligation-bearing clause; names a right applicable law already confers rather than creating a contractual entitlement)
reason:
SUB-SENTENCE exclusion: the SEGMENT IS KEPT and yields item C10-03 from S2. This clause alone is excluded, alongside the separately-dispositioned orphan fragment S1a.

GROUND -- SAVINGS/RESERVATION PROVISION, AND IT IS STATED INDEPENDENTLY OF EVERY DOWNSTREAM PROBLEM. 'the other party reserves the right to challenge such disclosure UNDER APPLICABLE LAW' names a right APPLICABLE LAW ALREADY CONFERS; it does not create a contractual entitlement. That is the defining feature of this exclusion class, and it is the whole ground. Same class as C02-062 ('subject is an event, savings/interpretive'), C03-102 and C12-017 ('interpretive/savings provision; no obligation-bearing clause'). The clause preserves a pre-existing position rather than granting anything, so there is no contractual undertaking or permission for IR v1 to monitor -- nothing changes about what either party may do by virtue of this contract saying it.

SECTION 2.5 WAS CHECKED AND IS NOT THE GROUND, stated so the reasoning is not mistaken for a monitorable-stakes exclusion. Section 2.5 says 'reserves the right to' is not per se excluded, and this clause is in fact NARROW (a specific disclosure), has a correlative party, and -- unusually -- has OBSERVABLE STAKES stated in the very next sentence, since exercising it triggers S2's prohibition. THOSE STAKES ARE REAL AND THEY DO NOT RESCUE IT, and conflating the two is the specific error this paragraph exists to prevent: S2's consequence is a fact about what follows from EXERCISING a pre-existing legal right, NOT evidence that S1b GRANTS anything. A savings provision that recites a right with real-world consequences is still a savings provision. Had section 2.5 been the ground, this clause would plausibly have survived it.

THE TAXONOMY PROBLEM WAS NOTICED AND IS EXPLICITLY SET ASIDE AS NOT THE DECIDING FACTOR. Recorded at the reviewer's direction, precisely to guard against a motivated-reasoning risk the drafter flagged before the ruling rather than after. The facts: 'challenge' has NO defensible taxonomy verb -- CHALLENGE, DISPUTE, OBJECT and CONTEST are ALL absent from ast.py's closed 34-verb ACTIONS (verified by execution, not from memory), and the one near precedent, E08-04's 'dispute amounts' -> PROCESS, does not extend, since under section 8.8.2's same-performance test processing is not contesting. So an item here would have carried action_not_in_taxonomy with an essentially arbitrary singleton -- exactly the cost section 8.8's own sub-choice paragraph complains about.

  WHY THAT IS NOT THE GROUND, AND WHY THE ORDER MATTERS. A taxonomy-coverage problem is a fact about IR v1's expressiveness; ELIGIBILITY is a question about whether the clause is obligation-bearing at all. Letting the first answer the second would exclude clauses for being HARD, which is precisely what section 2.1 step 4's rejection sample exists to catch, and it would set a precedent that any off-taxonomy verb can be dodged by reclassifying its clause. THE ELIGIBILITY QUESTION IS ANSWERED ON ITS OWN MERITS ABOVE, and would be answered the same way if 'challenge' were a taxonomy member tomorrow. The taxonomy problem is recorded as CONSISTENT WITH the exclusion -- a clause that grants nothing unsurprisingly has no act to map -- and as NOT ITS CAUSE.

NOT A DIFFICULTY DODGE. The segment is KEPT and an item is drawn from it; the excluded clause is not the segment's only content, and S2 (the item that survives) carries its own genuinely hard, untagged temporal gap rather than being the easy half. The cheaper move would have been to exclude the whole segment on S1a's orphan-fragment ground, which section 2.6 forbids since C13-017.

span_text: provided that the Quality Agreement may be amended if mutually agreed by the Parties.
rule: section 2 (savings/reservation provision -- states a power that exists by default, creating no new contractual entitlement)
reason:
SUB-SENTENCE exclusion: the SEGMENT IS KEPT and yields items E03-04 and E03-05 from the same sentence's two limbs. This proviso alone is excluded.

GROUND. 'the Quality Agreement may be amended if mutually agreed by the Parties' states a power THE PARTIES ALREADY HAVE: any contract may be amended by the mutual agreement of its parties, with or without a clause saying so. It creates no new contractual entitlement, so there is no future state for IR v1 to monitor -- nothing either party may do changes by virtue of this sentence.

THE TEST, AS THE REVIEWER STATED IT WHEN CONFIRMING THIS EXCLUSION: DOES REMOVING THE CLAUSE CHANGE WHAT EITHER PARTY COULD ALREADY DO? Here, no. That test generalises the class cleanly and is recorded here in those terms.

CLASS AND PRECEDENT. Same class as C02-062, C03-102 and C12-017 (interpretive/savings provisions), and a direct extension of C10-025#savings-proviso, ruled two segments earlier in this same batch -- 'names a right applicable law already confers rather than creating a contractual entitlement'. THE EXTENSION IS ACKNOWLEDGED AS SUCH rather than presented as settled law: the C10-025 ruling was made on 2026-09-24 and this is its first application, so it was put to the reviewer explicitly rather than applied by the drafter on its own authority.

SECTION 2.5 IS NOT THE GROUND, and the distinction matters. 'if mutually agreed by the Parties' would also support a section 2.5.1 reading (mutual consent leaves no reviewable standard), but that is not why this excludes -- a MAY clause with unreviewable discretion is excluded for having no monitorable stakes, whereas this one is excluded for granting nothing in the first place. The savings ground is prior and is the one relied on.

THIS EXCLUSION IS LOAD-BEARING FOR ELIGIBILITY, AND THAT IS DISCLOSED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE INFERRED. With the proviso excluded the segment carries 2 obligation-bearing clauses; with it kept, 3 -- both within section 2's 1-3 band, so the exclusion does NOT rescue the segment from the band. (The count would reach 4 and exceed the band only if S2's duty were ALSO annotated, which section 4.3.1 step 2 independently forbids.) Stated so a future reader can see the exclusion was not reached for to make a count work: it changes 3 to 2, and 3 was already eligible.

NOT A DIFFICULTY DODGE. The proviso is the easiest span in the segment; the two items that survive carry the harder content (an off-taxonomy collective-duty verb, a corpus artifact spliced into a defined term, a shared-subject split, and two vague-qualified triggers).
